question: Can Rumi work in isiZulu, isiXhosa and Sesotho?
governing_thought: Yes, with three conditions. Automated tests in all three languages show Rumi planning lessons, transcribing classrooms, drafting coaching and replying in voice notes; the first native listeners found its voice understandable, not yet natural.

conditions: Transcription uses the engine that scored best for each language; each page names it.
A first-language speaker reviews every lesson, transcript and voice before a teacher sees it. Only the isiZulu voice has had a first listen; no lesson or transcript on this site has been checked yet.

Coaching feedback reads as understandable, not natural (AI-judged 5.0, 2.5 and 5.0 out of 10 for isiZulu, isiXhosa, Sesotho), and so does the voice: a machine recovers the words, but two first-language isiZulu speakers from the coalition (9 October) heard pitch in the wrong places, sentence openings that start wrong, a greeting pitched as no speaker would pitch it, one line whose meaning was lost, and more English words than a teacher would use. Afrikaans was the one voice a listener on that call praised (a listener who speaks Afrikaans). Until first-language ratings pick a voice, every voice here is a draft: a blind review of four to six voices per language, with intonation-tuned variants where they kept the words right, is open, and native ratings decide.

legend.measured: a script compared Rumi's output with a known-good reference
legend.AI-judged: a second AI model judged it; never decides a verdict. The AI-judged nativeness scores of the voices were removed on 13 October: the first native listeners showed them to be wrong
legend.native ear pending: the first native listeners heard the isiZulu voice on 9 October (understandable, not yet natural); no other output on this site has been checked by a first-language speaker yet
legend.verdict: GREEN: every test run scored 7 or more out of 10. AMBER: one landed between 4 and 7. RED: one fell below 4. Rounding always goes against us: scores are cut down, error rates up.
